source.title: Structural Disentanglement in Bilinear MLPs via Architectural Inductive Bias
source.authors: Ojasva Nema; Kaustubh Sharma; A. Chauhan; Parikshit Pareek

record.tranche_reason: The paper cites work on grokking but does not measure delayed generalization, training-versus-test accuracy over time, or the delay’s dependence on dataset size. Its experiments instead examine learned operator structure and extrapolation under recursive composition.
record.gate_note: The paper reports structural and extrapolation results on algorithmic tasks, but does not test grokking dynamics or any other listed version. The results below are related findings that do not measure the behaviors named in those versions.
record.test_reason: The paper cites grokking work (Power et al., Nanda et al., Gromov) only as motivation. It trains bilinear, gated and pointwise MLPs and reports final operator structure, unlearning and recursive-extrapolation results. It reports no training-versus-test accuracy over time, no delayed generalization and no dependence on training-set size. The modular-arithmetic runs use a 90/10 split, outside the small-data grokking regime. They stop early at 99.9% validation accuracy, and per-architecture accuracies are not reported. Its Fourier-entropy and SVD measures describe the end-of-training logit table, not the time course of circuit formation or an identified algorithm.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that explicit multiplicative interactions yield structurally disentangled operators aligned with the algebraic ground truth, enabling surgical unlearning and stable long-horizon extrapolation. They argue that editability and generalization are constrained by representational structure set by architecture. They make no claims about grokking dynamics.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares bilinear and gated multiplicative architectures with pointwise networks on operator structure, unlearning, and recursive extrapolation. It does not reproduce the original grokking training setup or measure grokking.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture changes the reported structural and recursive-extrapolation outcomes; the paper does not test sensitivity of grokking delays.

fits_no_version.finding: On the cyclic successor task (N=400), multiplicative models keep accuracy under recursive composition to about k≈80; pointwise models collapse below k<10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multiplicative architectures learn transition operators that remain accurate under long-horizon composition better than pointwise MLPs.

fits_no_version.finding: On modular addition and multiplication over Z97 (and Z113 in the appendix), multiplicative models' interaction matrices have Fourier entropy near log p and steep SVD decay. ReLU and Sigmoid show low entropy, and Tanh shows diffuse spectra.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architectural inductive bias determines whether learned modular-arithmetic operators align with the ground-truth Fourier or low-rank structure.

record.problems: The paper does not measure grokking or provide training-versus-test accuracy time courses. For the related extrapolation results, the text gives no uncertainty estimates or individual numeric composition depths for all architectures; some outcomes are only described qualitatively or shown in figures. The theoretical analysis also relies on idealized gradient-flow, squared-loss, and small-initialization assumptions, as the authors note.
record.rows_left_out: Unlearning, Lie-group dynamics, and other results were left out because they do not measure the grokking or algorithmic generalization behaviors named in the claim versions.

untested.parts: Delayed test-accuracy jump after training saturation; delay versus training-set size.
Gradual circuit formation, removal of memorization, progress measures over training.
Delays on non-algorithmic data; control via initialization scale or weight norm.
Delayed generalization in LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
Weight-decay efficiency account, critical dataset size, ungrokking.
Whether runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm. Only architecture-level spectral differences are reported, with no mechanism identification or seed comparison.
Optimizer or numerical artifacts producing the delay.

record.verdict_notes: One could argue that the architecture-dependent Fourier structure on modular addition bears on V6. It is not linked here because the paper identifies no algorithm, compares no seeds and reports no per-architecture generalization accuracy. Appendix E.2 (Z113) replicates the spectral results but is equally off-claim.

versions.untested_parts: Delayed test-accuracy increase after training accuracy saturates, chance-level test accuracy during overfitting, and delay versus training-set size.
Gradual formation of a generalizing circuit, later removal of memorizing components, and continuous progress measures anticipating a test-accuracy jump.
Grokking-like delays on non-algorithmic data and switching them through initialization scale or weight norm.
Delayed generalization during realistic LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
A low-norm efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking below that size.
Whether runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm.
Whether optimizer or numerical choices produce the delay, or controlling them removes it.
